PullRequest.Title: Cache chat input picker measurements during resize
PullRequest.Body:

Part of #339863. This is the first of two input-picker optimizations; it does not address transcript or Sessions grid costs.

## Changes

- Separate intrinsic measurement, a pure fitting decision, and application of changed presentation states.
- Lazily cache expanded/compact/minimal width thresholds. Repeated resizes reuse those thresholds instead of expanding live controls and rebuilding measurement clones.
- Invalidate on item identity/membership, content including shorter labels, action/presentation state, overflow policy, configuration, fonts, theme, zoom, and visibility transitions.
- Coalesce parent/observer notifications without a resize-end debounce. Ignore the fitter's own presentation mutations.
- Preserve the existing fitting tolerance and compaction priority. Hidden, inert measurement lanes are siblings of the live lane so ancestor-dependent toolbar CSS remains effective.
- Preserve legacy picker-only fitting budgets for shrinkable lanes and actual truncation inside constrained inner toolbars.

No new settings, fixed picker widths, Sessions imports, or changes to keyboard/ARIA behavior.

## Validation

Source base: `d070672faea9561775af68832bc9fd536fb077c3`. This PR's corrected head: `4878845cece3be1d689c4e8ee7085987ac0eaa78`.

```sh
npm run transpile-client
# Passed.

./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputPickerResponsiveLayout.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputPickerActionItem.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/toolbar/toolbar.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerPresentation.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerActionItem.test.ts
# 85 passing on this cache-only revision.

npm run typecheck-client
# Passed on the final combined stack.

git diff --check && git diff --cached --check
# Passed.
```

The three cache-layer files also passed the final combined stack's ten-file ESLint command recorded in #340156. Hosted Compile & Hygiene, platform tests, and component checks pass on this PR; the external VS Code PR Check remains pending.

### Screenshot regressions fixed, not accepted

The first screenshot run exposed changed compaction with trailing fixed actions and constrained nested toolbars. Three new regression tests fail against the previous SHA-verified cached fitter and pass with the correction.

[Corrected component run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37541330053): **1,483 renders, zero errors, all 73 blocking fixtures unchanged; 102 Playwright fixture tests passed**. All five previously changed picker variants match the original baseline PNGs byte-for-byte, including provider icons and configured-model cases. No screenshot hashes were changed.

The remaining informational differences are seven pre-existing animated fixtures and an unrelated auto-visible scrollbar thumb whose PR image matches the earlier main baseline and previous PR run.

### Final-stack native evidence

Actual Code OSS plus `@hediet/dbgjs@0.1.0-nightly.34970595271` was rerun after the correction, on final stack head `91b68e844b85940ed9dd55e84c1f13042f41cd30`. **These numbers include #340156's suspension and are not a cache-only attribution.**

The comparison used an unoptimized source-equivalent baseline at `d070672f`, 1/3/6 production panes with eight deterministic turns each, a draft/selection, real native bounds changes and sash drags. Two repetitions per revision in ABBA order; each case requested 180 updates at 16ms spacing. The shared OS lock covered each complete app/debugger lifecycle. Timings were untraced/unprofiled, with counter wrappers removed and the dbgjs target released; diagnostic counters and trace were collected separately.

| Populated panes | Mixed resize: layouts / delivered resize, original to final stack | p95 rAF gap, original to final stack |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 16.9-17.1 to 11.2-11.6 | 16.7-16.9 to 16.7 ms |
| 3 | 50.7 to 28.5-28.6 | 41.6-42.1 to 33.3-33.6 ms |
| 6 | 126.3-127.8 to 56.3-56.5 | 91.4-100.2 to 67.6-76.9 ms |

Warm one- and three-pane diagnostic resize runs performed **zero intrinsic measurements, clone reconstruction, or presentation writes**. Six-pane runs performed three measurements/six clones/eighteen presentation writes, versus 768-840 measurements/clones before.

Matched geometry/presentation/ARIA/draft/focus/cursor/history checks passed. All **39 input-height changes** during native/sash resize and typing synchronously updated transcript sizing. Keyboard picker interaction, hidden/resume recovery and disposal passed.

The six-pane frame budget is not solved. Two repetitions show variability, not statistical confidence. Native fixtures do not use authenticated provider catalogues; those visual states are covered by the real-CSS tests and CI fixtures. Both builds emit development transcript/menu listener-threshold warnings; the aggressive correctness smoke had ten ResizeObserver-loop warnings, while the four scored matrix lifecycles had none.

## Manual checks

1. Open populated Chat/Agents panes and resize the native window and grid sashes continuously across compact/minimal boundaries, then widen again.
2. Change picker content and action availability, including a shorter label; change theme or zoom. Confirm fitting refreshes rather than retaining old widths.
3. Type a multiline draft during resizing. Confirm focus/selection survive and the input and transcript settle together.
4. Open a picker with the keyboard, navigate it, and dismiss it with Escape.
5. Check provider-icon and configured-model pickers in compact inputs and inside constrained toolbars.

## Stack

- This PR: intrinsic measurement caching, based on `main`.
- Follow-up: #340156 adds opt-in suspension of hidden picker/toolbar measurement, based on this branch.
- The correction was merged normally into the upper branch; neither branch was force-pushed.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each ResizeObserver delivery synchronously reran collection-wide picker expansion, geometry reads, deep DOM cloning, clone attachment, and layout measurement, with additional measurement passes for compact/minimal states. The work repeated throughout continuous resizing and multiplied across visible chat panes.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Continuous native-window or grid-sash resizing incurred repeated synchronous DOM cloning and layout resolution per picker lane, scaling with resize notifications, picker presentations, and visible chat panes and producing resize-frame latency/jank.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new layout path stores intrinsic presentation thresholds in _measurement, computes additional steps only until each bounded presentation is measured once, and then serves subsequent resize widths with fit() plus presentation updates; parent notifications are also coalesced onto animation frames.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, the ResizeObserver callback at line 60 called layout() for every observed size change. The deleted layout path reset every picker to expanded and repeatedly called _fitsAvailableWidth; that helper synchronously read live geometry and called _measurePreferredLayout, which deep-cloned and attached the lane for each presentation tried. The changed tests establish the intended multiplicity by asserting that subsequent width changes add zero cloneNode calls after threshold construction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continuously resize the native window or drag a grid sash with one or more visible, populated chat input panes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A lane's ResizeObserver can call layout synchronously with the delivered border-box width; parent ChatInputPart layout notifications are coalesced to an animation-frame callback. On a warm cache, fit() and any necessary presentation-state updates are on the resize critical path, while clone-based intrinsic measurement is absent unless the cache was invalidated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On a cold lane, deep-clone the picker subtree into preferred/minimum variants, attach both hidden clones, and synchronously read their geometry to construct bounded presentation thresholds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold cache: at most one measurement per reachable expanded/compact/minimal presentation step for the lane, bounded by picker count; each step creates two subtree clones. Warm cache: zero clones or clone geometry reads across arbitrary resize notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every resize layout restored expanded controls and repeatedly called the fitting helper, which created and measured a hosted deep clone for each presentation tried; no thresholds survived to the next resize.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold threshold construction blocks that lane's layout; after construction, resize progress no longer waits for clone creation or intrinsic geometry measurement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resize notification frequency multiplied by visible chat panes and their primary/secondary picker lanes; cold threshold count scales with effective responsive picker presentations, typically a small toolbar-sized collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each primary and secondary lane serializes itself with _isLayouting and allows at most one queued parent layout through MutableDisposable. Different lanes and panes can still run in the same frame; there is no global limiter, but warm work is bounded to one fit per delivered width and one queued callback per lane.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Thresholds are lazy and positive-only; width changes reuse them. Item identity/membership, observed content/attributes, relevant visibility transitions, theme/product-icon/configuration notifications, fonts, and zoom clear the cache. Invalidations coalesce through one scheduled callback; there is no miss coalescing across distinct lanes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the ResizeObserver, parent scheduling path, cache guard, bounded presentation loop, clone attachment, and geometry reads are explicit in the changed code and tests assert no repeated cloneNode calls on warm resizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame cost depends on picker subtree complexity, pane count, browser layout cost, and whether a resize follows an invalidation. Warm-path reduction is certain; precise milliseconds and largest real provider catalogs are not established by repository code alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. The diff removes the prior repeated clone/layout mechanism from warm continuous resizing, bounds cold work by presentation count, and coalesces parent notifications. The newly added second cold clone is a bounded tradeoff needed to cache both preferred and minimum sizing and does not establish a realistic net regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change picker labels/actions or trigger theme, product-icon theme, configuration, font-load, zoom, or hidden-to-visible transitions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The notification clears cached thresholds and schedules one animation-frame layout. The next connected, positive-width layout must rebuild thresholds before selecting and applying a presentation; repeated notifications before that callback do not create additional scheduled work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invalidate cached intrinsic widths, deep-clone each affected lane's toolbar subtree for preferred/minimum measurements, attach hidden clones, and resolve DOM geometry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One rebuild per live affected lane for a coalesced notification burst, with up to the bounded number of responsive presentation steps. Subsequent layouts remain warm until another substantive invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The lane remeasured on every mutation-triggered or explicit layout regardless of prior content identity; global theme/configuration/font/zoom listeners were not needed because no intrinsic cache survived between calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The rebuild occurs before the affected lane can choose its authoritative presentation after the content/style change; it is deferred to the scheduled frame unless an explicit synchronous layout flushes it first.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live chat panes and two possible lanes per pane, times responsive item/presentation count; notification bursts are reduced to one rebuild per lane per frame.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Invalidations coalesce per lane, including repeated invalidate() calls. Global notifications can wake every live lane in the target window in the same frame, with no cross-widget limiter; each lane remains internally serialized and performs only one cache rebuild for the coalesced burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Observed net-zero attribute writes are filtered, lane width/height style changes do not invalidate intrinsic sizes, and self-authored mutations are excluded while the observer is disconnected. Child/text changes and substantive attributes invalidate. There is no retained negative entry: disconnected or zero-width lanes clear state and retry after reconnect/visibility recovery.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all invalidation sources, mutation filtering, cache resets, and scheduling are explicit, and tests cover content growth/shrink, styles, font/zoom, visibility, coalescing, cancellation, and disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository evidence does not establish how often broad configuration events or late font loads occur with many simultaneous panes. The aggregate same-frame burst is real but bounded and infrequent enough that it does not meet the threshold for a regression finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Cache invalidation adds bounded cold clone work and broad listeners, but coalescing, mutation filtering, disposal, and the elimination of repeated warm measurements prevent unbounded or hot repeated work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and initially render a chat input, including primary and optional secondary picker lanes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction installs observers/listeners but does not immediately clone or measure. Initial picker layout is scheduled for the current/next animation frame; once connected and nonzero-width, cold threshold construction and presentation application must complete for responsive fitting to settle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build responsive item descriptors, deep-clone the lane for intrinsic sizing, attach hidden sibling clones, and synchronously read layout geometry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per initially visible lane, then cached. A typical widget has one primary and at most one secondary lane; work scales linearly with simultaneously created panes and bounded picker presentations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ChatInputPart called both lane layout methods synchronously during setup, and each call used live expansion and clone measurement without retaining thresholds for later layouts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred from synchronous widget setup to the animation-frame layout, but it must finish before initial responsive presentation is finalized.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chat widgets created concurrently, up to two lanes per widget, and responsive presentations per lane.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One scheduled callback per lane; primary and secondary lanes, and separate widgets, may initialize in the same frame. Each lane is serialized and its threshold loop is bounded by its responsive items.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Initial state is cold. The completed measurement remains owned by the lane until a substantive invalidation; disposal cancels a queued callback and releases observers/listeners/state. No cross-widget cache is used because measurements depend on each lane's DOM and ancestor styles.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed setup calls scheduleLayout(), the constructor and disposal ownership are visible, and tests verify queued-work cancellation and detached/reconnected behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of simultaneous widgets and cloned subtree size varies by product configuration. The code establishes bounded startup/render work but not a measurable startup regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Initial work remains bounded and is moved out of synchronous setup, while the resulting cache removes repeated later measurement.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and every diff page. Traced resize, initial render, invalidation, scheduling, DOM clone/layout, cache lifetime, concurrency, and disposal paths; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, or serialization boundary is reached. No diff-introduced high-confidence performance issue was found. Recorded the PR's concrete fix for the prior per-resize repeated DOM measurement regression.
